title: Transformations of graphs

points.text: Reflections in the x-axis and y-axis
Composite transformations and why order matters

bigPicture: Transformations let you sketch a new graph from a known one. Changes outside f act on y as written; changes inside act on x in the opposite way.

keyIdeas.cue: Effect of f(x) + b and f(x − a)?

keyIdeas.answer: Reflection in the x-axis; reflection in the y-axis.
Vertical stretch factor p; horizontal stretch factor 1/q.
Yes, e.g. stretch then translate differs from translate then stretch. Track a point through each step.

workedExamples.title: Track a point
workedExamples.prompt: (2, 5) is on y = f(x). Find its image on y = 3f(x − 1) − 2.

misconceptions.right: Horizontal stretch factor ½ (IB says stretch, not 'compression').

practice.prompt: Describe fully a sequence of transformations mapping y = x² onto y = 2(x + 1)² − 3.
practice.answer: Left 1; vertical stretch ×2; down 3 (stretch before the down shift)

practice.prompt: Sketch y = ln x and y = −ln(x − 2) on the GDC and state the asymptote of the second.

assessmentNote: AA SL external exams: Paper 1 without a calculator and Paper 2 with a GDC, both written answers in sections A (short) and B (extended); no multiple choice. Practice prompts here are original and are not predictions of exam questions.

memorise: All six transformation rules (none are in the booklet)
formulaBooklet.note: 'Given' = appears in the SL or prior-learning sections of the official AA formula booklet (2021 edition), which is provided in both papers. The ISL one-page sheet (Jan 2026) is a third-party summary of the same SL formulas; use the official booklet in the exam. 'Memorise' = needed but not printed.
